sanskrit_verse: कश्चित् कृत्वात्मनश् चिह्नं द्वेषात् परम् उपद्रवेत्। हेत्वर्थगतिसामर्थ्यैस् तत्र युक्तं परीक्षणम्॥
transliteration: kaścit kṛtvātmanaś cihnaṃ dveṣāt param upadravet | hetvarthagatisāmarthyais tatra yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When one marks oneself falsely out of hatred and thereby causes harm to another, investigation must proceed through capacity, intent, and causal adequacy.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the factual alignment of consciousness, not emotional impulse.
Causation is determined by the adequacy of means, motive, and opportunity.
Capacity-based responsibility requires examination of both intent and instrumental access.
Restoration logic demands reversal of distorted identity markers imposed on others.
Consciousness alignment necessitates correction of false attribution and reactive distortion.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a claimant has falsely marked their identity AND caused measurable disturbance to another's integrity THEN initiate reversal protocol through source-intent analysis.
IF emotional distortion (dveṣa) is detected as primary motivator THEN assess causal chain for instrumental misappropriation.
IF no adequate means exist for claimed action THEN invalidate liability attribution.
IF false identification leads to reputational harm THEN execute identity restoration before adjudicative conclusion.
IF reactive consciousness overrides discriminative awareness THEN assign completion process to restore clarity.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that mere allegation without instrumental capacity and causal adequacy cannot sustain liability. The threshold of responsibility lies in demonstrable alignment between intent, means, and effect. Emotional motivation alone does not constitute legal agency; therefore, higher courts must ensure investigations employ pramāṇa-based verification rather than subjective inference.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa here includes hetu (logical reason), artha (intended object), and gati (causal flow). Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that disturbance arises only when intent aligns with instrumental capacity. Therefore, proportional responsibility is assigned not to punish but to restore clarity where distortion occurred. Non-punitive reality rule holds that suffering results from misalignment, not judicial imposition.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Consciousness Re-alignment Process to dissolve reactive identity overlays.
Deploy Identity Restoration Protocol to reverse false markings and reputational distortions.
Assign Completion Process to responsible party for full assumption of energetic consequence.
Activate Instrumental Misuse Review to reclaim displaced capacities and prevent recurrence.
Execute Clarity Restoration Sequence to dissolve perceptual distortions induced by hatred.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: This law restores Dharma through consciousness-realized justice, wherein reality itself adjudicates, and punitive imagination dissolves. All beings are absolved through awakened clarity.
